6	Read the surah as one text and write its map of image chains: the lexical images that run through several of
7	its ayat and join them into one scene, process or movement. A later writer will read one ayah at a time, with
8	only that ayah's own dictionary. The map lets that writer hear what the ayah's words carry in the surah as a
9	whole, including senses whose evidence sits under the words of other ayat.
10	
11	Your evidence is the surah text, the dictionary of every root in the surah (each branch with the classical
12	dictionaries' own phrases), an earlier reader's channel review (channels.md),
13	and your own knowledge of Arabic and the Quran. Where a member or passage comes from memory rather than from
14	the dictionary or the text, say so. Do not delegate, browse or inspect files; run only the command the header describes.
15	
16	The channel review is an earlier reader's proposal. Ignore its judgements: grades,
17	strength or confidence labels, reading types, words such as "surprising", "exploratory" or "latent", and every
18	statement of what a reading may or may not do. Make your own judgement from the surah's words, the dictionary
19	phrases and the Quran. Do not rediscover what it already assembled: start from its chains, test each one
20	against the dictionary phrases and the text, and join, extend, split or correct them. Where its wording
21	abstracts a member, go back to the dictionary phrase and name what it actually says.
22	
23	A chain belongs on the map when its members are senses the dictionary attests for words that stand in the surah,
24	and together they make one image or process that the surah's wording or sequence lets a listener hear. A member
25	need not be the sense that translates its word in its own ayah; a chain is heard across the surah, not in one
26	word. A chain may join a sense and its reversal as well as the parts of one scene. Mark a member attested only
27	inside a fixed expression [fixed expression]; add no other label to a member or a chain, and where a source
28	records a phrase and rejects it, say so of that phrase alone. When the dictionary itself joins two of the
29	surah's words in one phrase, quote that phrase: it is the strongest evidence a chain can have. Keep a scene at
30	the level of its objects, their parts and their operation. When proposals share members, do not fold one into
31	another's more abstract function unless nothing concrete is lost. Carry every chain that meets this test,
32	however unusual; leave out proposals that do not.
33	
34	Write the map in English, with Arabic quoted exactly (surah wording from the text, dictionary phrases from the
35	dictionary). It is working material for the writer, not commentary prose.
36	
37	1. `## Chains`. For each chain, a `###` heading naming the image. One paragraph on what the image is and how it
38	   moves through the surah. Then its members, one line each: the ayah ref, the word as it stands in the text,
39	   the root and branch id, the dictionary's own phrase quoted exactly, and what this member contributes to the
40	   image. Add Quran passages outside the surah, with exact refs, where they stage or confirm the chain; for
41	   each, name the speaker and the situation in a few words, and include the ayah that opens its scene when the
42	   passage continues one.
43	2. `## Interactions`. Where chains meet: a shared member, a dictionary phrase that joins members of two chains,
44	   a Quran passage that stages two chains together, or one chain's scene needing another's. One line each: the
45	   chains, where they meet, the evidence.
46	3. `## Ayat`. For each ayah in order: the chains its words take part in, what its words add to each, and in one
47	   line the whole scene each chain makes across the surah, so that a writer who sees only this ayah sees the
48	   scene, not a fragment.
49	4. `## Not carried`. Each channel subchannel you did not carry into a chain: one short line
50	   each, its name and why, no prose.
51	
52	No ranking and no labels of strength or confidence. No list of what a writer must include. There is no length
53	target and no required number of chains or members.

# Surah 97: map of image chains

## Chains

### 1. Sent down from above, coming down in stages, ending in a rising

The surah opens with a single causative sending (أَنزَلْنَٰهُ, 97:1: "We sent it down", a completed act) and comes back to the same root in 97:4 as a continuing self-movement (تَنَزَّلُ, a present tense in the tafaʿʿul form: "they come down, stage after stage"). The dictionary separates the two: إنزال as sending a thing down, التنزل as "النزول في مهلة", coming down slowly, and التنزيل as what comes "مفرقا ومرة بعد أخرى". So the vertical line has a top (رَبِّهِم, the source of the leave), a downward movement in two forms (one sending, then a stream of descents), a receptacle (فِيهَا, the night), and an end that turns the direction round: مَطْلَعِ, a root whose base is "ظهور وبروز" and which also means climbing a mountain. The surah begins with something coming down into the dark and ends with something coming up out of it.
- 97:1 أَنزَلْنَٰهُ — ن ز ل B001 — "النزول في الأصل هو انحطاط من علو" (mufradat): the base movement from height to below; what is sent comes from above.
- 97:1 أَنزَلْنَٰهُ — ن ز ل B002 — "إما بإنزال الشيء نفسه كإنزال القرآن وإما بإنزال أسبابه" (mufradat): the causative, sending the Quran itself down; the dictionary names the Quran under this branch.
- 97:4 تَنَزَّلُ — ن ز ل B001 — "التنزل النزول في مهلة" (sihah): the descent in 97:4 is gradual, unhurried, spread over the night.
- 97:4 تَنَزَّلُ — ن ز ل B002 — "التنزيل يختص بما أنزل مفرقا ومرة بعد أخرى" (mufradat): coming down in parts, one time after another; the angels come in wave after wave.
- 97:4 تَنَزَّلُ — ن ز ل B010 — "النزلة المرة الواحدة؛ ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى أي مرة أخرى" (ayn): a single descent counted as one event; the dictionary's example is the Prophet seeing the angel at "another descent".
- 97:4 تَنَزَّلُ — ن ز ل B001 — "نزل فلان عن الدابة أو من علو إلى سفل" (ayn): getting down from a mount, from high to low; the descending party arrives and dismounts (taken up in chain 8).
- 97:4 رَبِّهِم — ر ب ب B001 — "ويكون الرب: السيد المطاع" (tahdhib): the top of the line, the one whose leave starts the descent.
- 97:5 مَطْلَعِ — ط ل ع B001 — "أصل واحد صحيح يدل على ظهور وبروز" (maqayis): coming out and appearing, the reverse direction of نزول.
- 97:5 مَطْلَعِ — ط ل ع B006 — "طلعت الجبل إذا علوته؛ المطلع موضع الاطلاع من إشراف إلى الانحدار؛ وقد يكون المطلع المصعد" (tahdhib) [fixed expression]: مطلع as a place of climbing and of looking down; the closing word of the surah is a word of going up.

Passages:
- 53:13 وَلَقَدْ رَءَاهُ نَزْلَةً أُخْرَىٰ — God speaking of the Prophet's second sight of the angel (the scene starts at 53:1); quoted by the dictionary under B010.
- 17:105 وَبِٱلْحَقِّ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ وَبِٱلْحَقِّ نَزَلَ — God of the Quran: the causative and the intransitive forms side by side, as in 97:1 and 97:4.
- 17:106 وَقُرْءَانًۭا فَرَقْنَٰهُ ... وَنَزَّلْنَٰهُ تَنزِيلًۭا — God, answering the polytheists: a Quran divided up and sent down in stages.
- 25:32 لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ جُمْلَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ — the unbelievers ask for one single sending; God answers that it was sent in stages to make the heart firm.

### 2. The Spirit and the command: Lord, leave, bearers, every matter

97:4 is a chain of authority stated in order. The Lord (رَبِّهِم) gives leave (بِإِذْنِ). The bearers (ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ, a word the dictionary derives from ألوك, "message") and the Spirit (ٱلرُّوحُ, which the dictionary names as Jibrīl and also as the Quran itself) come down carrying "every matter" (مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍۢ). The dictionary joins several of these words to one another. Its phrase under إذن glosses بإذني as "بأمري". Its phrase under أمر quotes "قل الروح من أمر ربي", joining روح, أمر and رب. Its phrase under إذن uses "أذنت لربها" for hearing with obedience. Its phrase under سلم defines إسلام as "الاستسلام لأمر الله". So the command comes down by leave, through bearers, and is answered at the bottom by hearing and yielding. 97:5's سلام carries that yielding sense under the greeting.
- 97:4 رَبِّهِم — ر ب ب B001 — "رب كل شئ: مالكه؛ وقد قالوه في الجاهلية للملك؛ رببت القوم: سستهم" (sihah): the owner and governor who sends; the suffix هم makes him the Lord of the descending angels themselves.
- 97:4 بِإِذْنِ — ء ذ ن B004 — "فعله بإذني أي بعلمي وهو في معنى بأمري" (ayn): leave is knowledge and command at once; the dictionary itself joins إذن to أمر.
- 97:4 بِإِذْنِ — ء ذ ن B004 — "بإذن الله أي بعلمه؛ ويكون بإذنه أي بأمره" (tahdhib): the same pairing.
- 97:4 بِإِذْنِ — ء ذ ن B004 — "الذي يأذن بالدخول" (ayn); "ائذن لي على الأمير؛ الآذن الحاجب" (sihah): leave as permission to go in to a ruler, given by a doorkeeper; the descent happens as entry by permission (taken up in chain 8).
- 97:4 بِإِذْنِ — ء ذ ن B002 — "وأذنت لربها أي سمعت سمع طاعة وقبول" (tahdhib): the dictionary joins أذن and رب; at root إذن is the ear and obedient hearing, and the command meets a listener.
- 97:4 ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ — م ل ك B009 — "أصله مألك بتقديم الهمزة من الألوك وهي الرسالة" (sihah): the angels are by name message-carriers; the descent is a delivery.
- 97:4 ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ — م ل ك B003 — "الملكوت ملك الله وملكوت الله سلطانه" (ayn): the root heard as sovereignty; the descent comes out of a kingdom.
- 97:4 ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ — م ل ك B005 — "ملاك الأمر ما يعتمد عليه" (ayn); "هذا ملاك الأمر وملاكه أي صلاحه" (tahdhib) [fixed expression]: the dictionary joins ملك and أمر: that on which an affair rests and is set right.
- 97:4 وَٱلرُّوحُ — ر و ح B002 — "الروح جبرئيل وهو روح القدس؛ الروح ملك يقوم وحده" (ayn): the Spirit as Jibrīl, named apart from the angels as one who stands alone; hence "the angels and the Spirit".
- 97:4 وَٱلرُّوحُ — ر و ح B002 — "يسمى القرآن روحا وكذلك جبريل وعيسى" (sihah): the Quran is also called روح; the bearer of 97:4 shares the name of what was sent down in 97:1 (the ـه of أنزلناه).
- 97:4 أَمْرٍ — ء م ر B010 — "قل الروح من أمر ربي أي من إبداعه" (mufradat): the dictionary joins روح, أمر and رب in one phrase; أمر here is God's own act of bringing into being.
- 97:4 أَمْرٍ — ء م ر B002 — "الأمر الذي هو نقيض النهي قولك افعل كذا" (maqayis): the command, "do this".
- 97:4 أَمْرٍ — ء م ر B001 — "الأمر الشأن وجمعه أمور" (mufradat): every affair or matter; what is carried down.
- 97:4 كُلِّ — ك ل ل B003 — "كل اسم موضوع للإحاطة مضاف أبدا" (maqayis): the cargo leaves nothing out.
- 97:5 سَلَٰمٌ — س ل م B003 — "الإسلام الاستسلام لأمر الله تعالى وهو الانقياد لطاعته والقبول لأمره" (ayn): the dictionary joins سلم and أمر; yielding to the command is the counterpart of the command that came down.
- 97:5 سَلَٰمٌ — س ل م B012 — "أسلم أمره إلى الله أي سلم" (sihah) [fixed expression]: handing one's affair over to God; again سلم with أمر.

### 3. Measure and decree, sent down by measure

قَدْر in the dictionary means first the full extent and limit of a thing ("مبلغ الشيء وكنهه ونهايته"), then God's decree that fixes things at their extents, then the act of measuring out and preparing. The dictionary joins it to the surah's other verb: "ينزل المطر بمقدار". The night's name is therefore a name of measuring and fixing. 97:4 carries "every matter" down. The dictionary also gives تنزيل as "ترتيب الشيء ووضعه منزله", putting each thing in its station. In this chain the descent hands out what the measure has fixed, each matter to its place. The Quran says it in nearly the surah's own words at 44:3–4 (sent down in a blessed night, "in it every wise matter is made distinct").
- 97:1 ٱلْقَدْرِ — ق د ر B001 — "مبلغ الشيء وكنهه ونهايته" (maqayis): the full extent and end-limit of a thing.
- 97:1 ٱلْقَدْرِ — ق د ر B001 — "القدر مبلغ الشيء؛ لكل شيء مقدار وأجل" (ayn): each thing has a measure and a term; the night as the night of measures and terms.
- 97:1 ٱلْقَدْرِ — ق د ر B001 — "المقدار هو الهنداز؛ ينزل المطر بمقدار" (tahdhib): the dictionary joins قدر and نزل; things come down by measure.
- 97:1 ٱلْقَدْرِ — ق د ر B002 — "قضاء الله تعالى الأشياء على مبالغها ونهاياتها" (maqayis): God decreeing things at their extents and limits.

- 97:1 ٱلْقَدْرِ — ق د ر B003 — "قدرة الله تعالى على خليقته" (maqayis): the power that carries the measure out.
- 97:1 أَنزَلْنَٰهُ / 97:4 تَنَزَّلُ — ن ز ل B004 — "التنزيل ترتيب الشيء ووضعه منزله" (maqayis): sending down as setting each thing in its station.
- 97:4 تَنَزَّلُ — ن ز ل B002 — "إنزال الله تعالى نعمه ونقمه على الخلق وإعطاؤهم إياها" (mufradat): what comes down is what is handed out to creatures, favour and punishment.
- 97:4 أَمْرٍ — ء م ر B001 — "الأمر واحد من أمور الناس" (ayn): the single affairs of people, each one measured.

### 4. Whole and parts: the joined whole and its dispensing

The dictionary explains two of the surah's words through one operation, ضمّ, putting parts together. For ألف (B002): "كل شيء ضممت بعضه إلى بعض فقد ألفته". For كل: "لفظ كل هو لضم أجزاء الشيء ويفيد معنى التمام". It explains ألف and تنزيل through ترتيب, ordering: "المؤلف ما جمع من أجزاء مختلفة ورتب ترتيبا", "التنزيل أيضا الترتيب". Against this joining stands the dictionary's other sense of تنزيل, "مفرقا ومرة بعد أخرى". So the surah lets one hear a whole put together and a whole handed out piece by piece. أنزلناه is the one act, and the ـه is the whole. تنزّل is the stream of parts. كل أمر is the parts that make up "every". ألف is a number that is itself a word of joining. قدر adds the fitting of each piece ("قدر في السرد أي أحكمه", fitting the rings of mail). 44:4's يُفْرَقُ (made distinct, parted out) is this chain's reverse word.

- 97:3 أَلْفِ — ء ل ف B002 — "ألفت بينهم تأليفا إذا جمعت بينهم بعد تفرق" (tahdhib): gathering after separation, the reverse of تفريق.

- 97:3 أَلْفِ — ء ل ف B002 — "المؤلف ما جمع من أجزاء مختلفة ورتب ترتيبا" (mufradat): different parts gathered and set in order.

### 5. Reckoning by nights, months and a thousand: the worth of one night

97:3 sets one night against a thousand months. Each word belongs to the lunar reckoning the dictionary records. The month is named for the new crescent and then counted as thirty days ("الشهر الهلال ثم سمي كل ثلاثين يوما باسم الهلال"). قدر gives the verb of counting the month out to thirty ("فاقدروا له أي أتموا ثلاثين"). ألف gives the verb of bringing a sum up to a thousand ("آلفت الدراهم أي بلغت بها الألف"), and that verb matches قدر's own definition, "مبلغ الشيء". ليل gives night as the unit and the darkest last night of the month. طلع gives the rising of the moon and stars. In the lunar day the night comes first, and the dictionary records that "this night" means the one coming. So 97:3 is a sum. A thousand months is about thirty thousand nights, and one night outweighs them. قدر is also worth or extent: the night's measure is greater than the count. نزل B003 ("المنزلة المرتبة") adds rank, and خير adds the chosen, better side of a comparison. The reckoning runs to the end of the surah: the count stops at a marked edge, حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ.
- 97:1 لَيْلَةِ — ل ي ل B001 — "ليل وليلة وليلات وليال" (maqayis; sihah; mufradat): ليلة as one counted unit of night.
- 97:1 لَيْلَةِ — ل ي ل B001 — "ليلة ليلى أشد ليلة في الشهر ظلمة وآخر ليلة فيه" (jamhara): the dictionary joins ليلة and شهر; the month's darkest and last night, the end of the lunar count.
- 97:2 لَيْلَةُ — ل ي ل B003 — "هذه الليلة التي في السماء أقرب الليالي من يومك وهي الليلة التي تليه" (tahdhib): "the night" names the night nearest to the day, the one that follows it; a night that keeps coming back in the reckoning.
- 97:2 لَيْلَةُ — ل ي ل B003 — "الهلال في هذه الليلة التي في السماء يعني الليلة التي تدخلها يتكلم بهذا في النهار" (tahdhib): the dictionary joins the night with the new crescent; the night is where the month is sighted.

### 6. Night split open by dawn

The surah starts in night and ends at the place or moment where the dawn comes up. The dictionary defines الفجر as the night being split. فجر is first water bursting out of a breach ("انفجر الماء انفجارا تفتح", "شق الشيء شقا واسعا"). Dawn is "انفجار الظلمة عن الصبح", and the mufradat joins the two surah words: "قيل للصبح فجر لكونه فجر الليل", dawn is called fajr because it splits the night. طلع is joined to فجر in the dictionary's own phrase, "طلع الفجر". مطلع is both the rising (مَطْلَع, the event) and the place of rising (مَطْلِع); the dictionary records the split and the Quran uses the place form at 18:90. So the image is a closed dark span, ليلة ليلاء, with سلام filling it (حَتَّىٰ marks its edge). At its edge the dark is broken from inside and light comes up through the break. The variant reading مَطْلِعِ (al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf; from memory) gives the place-sense.
- 97:1 لَيْلَةِ — ل ي ل B001 — "الليل خلاف النهار" (maqayis); "ظلام الليل" (tahdhib): night as the dark opposite of day, the closed span.

### 7. Hidden and shown: from "what will make you know" to the coming out

97:2 asks وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ, "what has made you know". The dictionary gives دراية as knowledge got by some skill or trick ("المعرفة المدركة بضرب من الحيل"). Another branch of the same root is the hunter's craft: hiding behind a decoy animal and looking for game one has not yet seen ("تدريت الصيد إذا نظرت أين هو ولم تره بعد"). The night is the hidden thing. Darkness covers it. Its knowledge comes by leave (إذن as "بعلمه"; إذن is also announcement, أذان). Its end is ظهور وبروز. The dictionary's phrases for طلع include inspecting what is inside a matter (اطلع على باطن أمره). شهر carries public clarity ("الشهرة وضوح الأمر") and the crescent becoming known. So the surah moves from a question about something out of sight, through a night that covers, to a coming-into-view at its end.

### 8. The guest who comes down: leave to enter, greeting, provision

نزل as the dictionary gives it is not only coming down. It is also getting off one's mount, setting down one's baggage at a place, and becoming a guest. النزيل is the guest, النزل is what is made ready for him, and أنزلت فلانا means "I hosted him". The surah lets this scene be heard. A company comes down by night (تَنَزَّلُ) and settles in a place (فِيهَا). They come by leave, and the dictionary's إذن includes the doorkeeper who gives leave to enter. The first word of 97:5 is سَلَٰمٌ, the greeting of an arriving guest or of a host, "السلام عليكم". The provision side lies in the night's own root. قدر gives "قدرت الشيء أي هيأته", preparing, which uses the same verb هيّأ the dictionary uses for the guest's meal ("النزل ما يهيأ للنزيل"). Under another vocalisation (قِدْر) the same root gives the cooking pot and the meat cooked in it. خير gives كرم and الهبة. The Quran stages angel-guests met with "سلام" at Abraham's door, and angels coming down (تتنزل) with a نُزُل, a guest's portion, from God.

### 9. A host that fills the earth

The angels of 97:4 come as a crowd. The plural, كل, and the ألف of the ayah before (heard again in 97:4) make the multitude. The dictionary joins the surah's رب root to ألف: "الربيون: الألوف", "الربي واحد الربيين، وهم الألوف من الناس". ألف itself has a verb for making a company a thousand strong. ك ل ل gives الكلاكل, troops. ط ل ع gives "طلاع الأرض ملؤها", enough to fill the earth. So the night is filled from the sky down to the ground with a coming host, counted in thousands and beyond count. The Quran stages exactly that: angels sent down in thousands (3:124, منزلين) to a people at war (taken up in chain 10). A hadith (from memory) says the angels on earth that night outnumber the pebbles.

### 10. A host comes down on a people by night and arrives at dawn: raid or peace

Arab war-poetry and the Quran know this scene: a force travels by night, falls on a people's camp (نزل بساحتهم), and strikes at first light. The surah has every piece of it: a company comes down at night, carries every matter, and stays until the rising of the dawn, the hour of the raid. The dictionary's branches give the attack itself. نزل is النازلة, the hard blow of fortune that "comes down on a people", and النزال, both sides coming down to fight. فجر has "انفجرت عليهم الدواهي", disasters bursting on them all at once. طلع has "طلع علينا فلان إذا هجم", appearing on us in attack, and الطليعة, the scouts sent ahead. دري has choosing a place to raid. ليل has the one who can bear the night march. Against all this the surah's word is سَلَٰمٌ: freedom from harm ("أن يسلم الإنسان من العاهة والأذى") and peace as the opposite of war ("السلم ضد الحرب"). What comes down that night is the reverse of a نازلة. The dictionary then ties war and the sacred months together: "سمت قريش هذه الحرب فجارا لأنها كانت في الأشهر الحرم", joining فجر and شهر. فجار is fighting that broke the sanctity of the months. The night of 97 is sacred time kept whole, peace until the dawn.

### 11. Rain sent down by measure: wind, cloud, burst water, what comes up

The dictionary's first examples of نزل and قدر are rain: "نزل المطر من السماء نزولا", "ينزل المطر بمقدار". The surah's other words supply the rest of a rain scene through their own branches. روح is wind and breeze. The رب root gives الرباب, layered low cloud, "سمي بذلك لأنه يرب النبات", and أربت السحابة, the cloud that stays. ك ل ل gives cloud lighting up with lightning. فجر is water bursting out of the ground. طلع is the palm's spathe and the crop showing above ground. أمر is increase and blessing. ملك says water is what keeps a matter going. The Quran often parallels rain and revelation, both "sent down by measure" from treasuries above. Here the descent of the Spirit and the angels through the night can be heard as a measured downpour that brings out growth at its rising.

### 12. Rest through the night: the evening return, the fold, safe until morning

روح in the dictionary has the evening return: الرواح is the time "من لدن زوال الشمس إلى الليل", and الإراحة is bringing the herd back in the evening to the مراح, "حيث تأوي الماشية بالليل". It has rest and catching one's breath after exhaustion. It has birds going back to their nests. ك ل ل gives the exhausted walker ("الكال المعيي"), the same word for exhaustion (الإعياء) that روح uses for the breath coming back. ألف gives the birds and doves that keep to a house. So الروح coming down at night brings the sense of coming home to rest. سَلَٰمٌ هِىَ is the fold kept safe from harm all night. حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ is the morning, when the herd goes out again ("سرحت الماشية بالغداة وراحت بالعشي").

### 13. Good that bursts out, and its reverse

فجر and خير meet in the dictionary's own phrase: "الفجر وهو الكرم والتفجر بالخير", "رجل ذو فجر إذا كان يتفجر بالخير". The surah sets خَيْرٌۭ in its middle and ٱلْفَجْرِ at its end. Heard together, the night's good bursts out like water and like the dawn, a generosity that overflows. The other branches add provision: the نزل as the yield and surplus of land, أمر as increase, روح as eagerness to give and as provision (ريحان), رب as favour. The same bursting has a dark side in the dictionary: فجور is the bursting out into sin ("الانبعاث والتفتح في المعاصي"), and الخير is defined against الشر. The surah's فجر is dawn and bounty, the reverse of فجور.

## Ayat

### 97:1 إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ فِى لَيْلَةِ ٱلْقَدْرِ
- Chain 1: أَنزَلْنَٰهُ is the one completed sending from above ("انحطاط من علو"), the Quran sent itself. Scene: sent down once from the Lord, then coming down in stages all night, ending in a rising at dawn.
- Chain 2: the ـه of أَنزَلْنَٰهُ shares the name روح with the bearer of 97:4 ("يسمى القرآن روحا"). Scene: the Lord gives leave, bearers of the message and the Spirit carry every command down, and it is met by yielding (سلام).
- Chain 3: ٱلْقَدْرِ is measure, extent and decree; أَنزَلْنَٰهُ adds sending by measure and setting in place ("التنزيل ترتيب الشيء ووضعه منزله"). Scene: in the night of measure every matter is fixed to its extent and sent down to its place.
- Chain 4: أَنزَلْنَٰهُ is the whole given in one act, against the parts of تَنَزَّلُ; قدر adds the fitting of each piece ("قدر في السرد أي أحكمه"). Scene: a whole joined part to part (ألف, كل) and given out part by part.
- Chain 5: لَيْلَةِ is the counted unit and ٱلْقَدْرِ the counting of the month out to thirty ("فاقدروا له"). Scene: one night weighed against a thousand months of nights and found greater, counted up to the dawn.
- Chain 6: لَيْلَةِ is the closed dark span. Scene: a night dark to the full, filled with peace, split open at its end by dawn coming up.
- Chain 7: the night as the covering dark. Scene: a hidden thing ("ما أدراك") covered by night, known only by leave, brought into view at the rising.
- Chain 8: أَنزَلْنَٰهُ also means lodging someone ("أنزلني منزلا مباركا"); ٱلْقَدْرِ adds preparing (هيّأ) and the cooking pot (قِدْر). Scene: guests come down at night, enter by leave, are greeted with سلام and given the portion made ready.
- Chain 10: لَيْلَةِ adds the night march ("سرى الليل"). Scene: a host comes down on a people by night and arrives at dawn, and brings peace, not the blow of a raid.
- Chain 11: أَنزَلْنَٰهُ and ٱلْقَدْرِ join in "ينزل المطر بمقدار". Scene: wind and low cloud, measured rain all night, water bursting out and crops showing at the rising.
- Chain 12: لَيْلَةِ is the span of rest. Scene: the evening return to the fold, rest after exhaustion, safekeeping all night, release at morning.

### 97:2 وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ
- Chain 7: أَدْرَىٰكَ is knowledge reached by skill ("بضرب من الحيل") and the hunter looking for game unseen ("نظرت أين هو ولم تره بعد"). Scene: a hidden thing covered by night, known only by leave, brought into view at the rising.
- Chain 5: the repeated لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ is again the counted night and its measure, and B003's "the night nearest your day" points to the coming night. Scene: one night weighed against a thousand months of nights, counted up to the dawn.
- Chain 3: the question asks after the night of measure and decree. Scene: in the night of measure every matter is fixed and sent down to its place.
- Chain 10: دري B002 "ادرى ... مكان كذا أي اعتمدوه بغزو أو غارة" [fixed expression], picking out a place to raid. Scene: a host comes down on a people by night and arrives at dawn, bringing peace instead of the raid.
- Chain 6: the night named again. Scene: a dark night filled with peace, split by dawn.

### 97:3 لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍۢ
- Chain 5: أَلْفِ (the number; "آلفت الدراهم أي بلغت بها الألف") and شَهْرٍ (crescent and thirty days); خَيْرٌۭ as the better, the chosen ("الاختيار طلب ما هو خير"). Scene: one night weighed against a thousand months of nights and found greater, counted up to the dawn.
- Chain 4: أَلْفِ as joining ("انضمام الشيء إلى الشيء", "المؤلف ما جمع من أجزاء مختلفة ورتب ترتيبا"). Scene: a whole joined part to part and given out part by part.
- Chain 9: أَلْفِ as making a company a thousand ("آلفت القوم صيرتهم ألفا"). Scene: a host counted in thousands fills the night down to the earth.
- Chain 10: شَهْرٍ in "الأشهر الحرم" (joined with الفجار) and "شهر سيفه" [fixed expression]; خَيْرٌۭ against شر. Scene: a host comes down by night and arrives at dawn, and the sacred time is kept in peace, not broken by war.
- Chain 8: خَيْرٌۭ as كرم and الهبة; أَلْفِ as being at ease with someone ("ألفت فلانا إذا أنست به"). Scene: guests come down at night, enter by leave, are greeted and given what is made ready.
- Chain 12: أَلْفِ as birds that keep to a house ("أوالف الحمام دواجنها التي تألف البيوت"). Scene: the evening return to the fold, rest, safekeeping all night, release at morning.
- Chain 13: خَيْرٌۭ as abundant good and wealth, which joins with فجر ("التفجر بالخير"). Scene: good bursting out like water and dawn, the reverse of فجور.
- Chain 7: شَهْرٍ as "الشهرة وضوح الأمر". Scene: the hidden thing brought into plain view at the rising.

### 97:4 تَنَزَّلُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍۢ
- Chain 1: تَنَزَّلُ is gradual descent ("النزول في مهلة"), in parts, time after time; رَبِّهِم is the top. Scene: sent down once, then coming down in stages all night, ending in a rising.
- Chain 2: every word: Lord, leave ("بإذني ... بأمري"), message-bearers (ملائكة from ألوك), the Spirit (Jibrīl; also the Quran), كل, أمر (with "قل الروح من أمر ربي"). Scene: the Lord gives leave, bearers carry every command down, and it is met by yielding (سلام).
- Chain 3: كُلِّ أَمْرٍۢ is each matter, measured; تَنَزَّلُ is handing out ("إنزال الله تعالى نعمه ونقمه"). Scene: every matter fixed to its extent and sent down to its place.
- Chain 4: تَنَزَّلُ is the parts of the whole ("مفرقا"), and كُلِّ is the joining of parts ("لضم أجزاء الشيء"). Scene: a whole joined part to part and given out part by part.
- Chain 5: أَمْرٍۢ as appointed time and marker ("الأمارة الموعد"). Scene: one night weighed against a thousand months, counted to the dawn.
- Chain 7: بِإِذْنِ as "بعلمه" and as making known (أذان). Scene: a hidden thing known only by leave, brought into view at the rising.
- Chain 8: تَنَزَّلُ is alighting, setting down baggage, being a guest; فِيهَا the lodging; بِإِذْنِ the doorkeeper's leave; وَٱلرُّوحُ "روح وريحان أي رحمة ورزق". Scene: guests come down at night, enter by leave, are greeted with سلام and given the portion made ready.
- Chain 9: ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ plural, كُلِّ ("لفظه واحد ومعناه جمع"), رَبِّهِم ("الربيون: الألوف"), الكلاكل. Scene: a host counted in thousands fills the night down to the earth.
- Chain 10: تَنَزَّلُ as النازلة and النزال. Scene: a host comes down on a people by night and arrives at dawn, bringing peace instead of the raid's blow.
- Chain 11: تَنَزَّلُ rain, وَٱلرُّوحُ wind, رَبِّهِم cloud (الرباب) that stays, كُلِّ the cloud lit by lightning, أَمْرٍۢ increase, ملك "الماء ملك أمر". Scene: wind and low cloud, measured rain all night, water bursting out and crops showing at the rising.
- Chain 12: وَٱلرُّوحُ as evening return, the night fold, breath after exhaustion, birds back to nests; كُلِّ as the exhausted ("الكال المعيي"). Scene: the evening return, rest, safekeeping all night, release at morning.
- Chain 13: نزل as yield and surplus, أمر as increase, روح as eagerness for good and provision, رب as favour. Scene: good bursting out like water and dawn, the reverse of فجور.

### 97:5 سَلَٰمٌ هِىَ حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ
- Chain 1: مَطْلَعِ is rising and climbing ("طلعت الجبل إذا علوته"), the reverse of نزول. Scene: sent down once, then coming down in stages all night, ending in a rising at dawn.
- Chain 2: سَلَٰمٌ as "الاستسلام لأمر الله" and "أسلم أمره إلى الله" [fixed expression]. Scene: the Lord gives leave, bearers carry every command down, and it is met by yielding.
- Chain 5: مَطْلَعِ as the risings of dawn, moon and star that mark the reckoning; حَتَّىٰ the edge. Scene: one night weighed against a thousand months, counted up to the dawn.
- Chain 6: ٱلْفَجْرِ splits the night ("قيل للصبح فجر لكونه فجر الليل"), water bursting through a breach; مَطْلَعِ the rising and its place ("طلع الفجر"). Scene: a night dark to the full, filled with peace, split open at its end by dawn coming up.
- Chain 7: مَطْلَعِ is "ظهور وبروز", looking inside a matter, showing the head. Scene: a hidden thing covered by night, known only by leave, brought into view at the rising.
- Chain 8: سَلَٰمٌ is the greeting of arrival and God's name, "وداره الجنة". Scene: guests come down at night, enter by leave, are greeted with سلام and given what is made ready.
- Chain 9: مَطْلَعِ "طلاع الأرض ملؤها" [fixed expression]. Scene: a host counted in thousands fills the night down to the earth.
- Chain 10: سَلَٰمٌ (free of harm; peace against war) stands against ٱلْفَجْرِ's "انفجرت عليهم الدواهي" [fixed expression], the الفجار fought in the sacred months, and مَطْلَعِ's "طلع علينا فلان إذا هجم" [fixed expression], the scouts and "هول المطلع" [fixed expression]. Scene: a host comes down on a people by night and arrives at the dawn hour of the raid, and what it brings is peace.
- Chain 11: ٱلْفَجْرِ as water bursting out and valley outlets; مَطْلَعِ as palm spathe and crop showing. Scene: wind and low cloud, measured rain all night, water bursting out and crops showing at the rising.
- Chain 12: سَلَٰمٌ as safekeeping and well-being; ٱلْفَجْرِ as the morning that lets the herd out. Scene: the evening return to the fold, rest after exhaustion, safekeeping all night, release at morning.
- Chain 13: ٱلْفَجْرِ as "الكرم والتفجر بالخير" and as فجور reversed. Scene: good bursting out like water and dawn, the reverse of فجور.
